svg.text: Allwinner A13 SBC: manufactured DDR copper vs. the benchmark's applied clearance
The original board does not keep the applied 0.200 mm clearance: 268 copper pairs on the 96 requested nets are closer, down to 0.1271 mm.
Closer than applied: 33 trace-to-ball, 59 trace-to-trace, 58 via-to-ball, 118 via-to-trace. Coupled differential-pair gaps (446 pairs) are excluded.
Source: vd-rd/sbc_allwinner_a13 @ 8973c32, hardware/module.kicad_pcb. Original copper is shown for reference only; the benchmark removes it and routes these nets again.
Requested DDR nets, original routing (both signal layers)
U200 top layer: shaded = no trace centre line allowed at 0.200 mm
One escape channel between two balls
Ball pitch 0.800 mm, ball 0.400 mm: 0.400 mm between balls.
A 0.1016 mm trace at 0.200 mm clearance needs
A 0.45 mm via between four balls needs 1.250 mm
of the 1.131 mm diagonal: does not fit.
The original trace keeps 0.1492 mm to each ball.
